definitions.explanation: the habit or act of eating food very quickly
competitive eating where participants race to consume food

examples.japanese: {早食|はやぐ}いは{体|からだ}に{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: Eating fast is bad for your health.

examples.japanese: {昼休|ひるやす}みが{短|みじか}いので、つい{早食|はやぐ}いになる。
examples.english: Because my lunch break is short, I tend to eat quickly.

examples.japanese: {早食|はやぐ}いを{直|なお}したいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I want to break my habit of eating fast.

examples.japanese: {早食|はやぐ}い{大会|たいかい}に{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: I participated in a speed-eating contest.

examples.japanese: ホットドッグの{早食|はやぐ}いで{新記録|しんきろく}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: A new record was set in the hot dog eating contest.

examples.japanese: {早食|はやぐ}い{競争|きょうそう}はかなり{危険|きけん}なスポーツだ。
examples.english: Competitive eating is quite a dangerous sport.

notes:
FORMS:
{早|はや}い (fast, quick) + {食|く}い (eating). The rendaku changes く to ぐ.

SENSE 1 — EATING QUICKLY:
A common bad habit. Health professionals warn that {早食|はやぐ}い is associated with {消化不良|しょうかふりょう} (indigestion) and {肥満|ひまん} (obesity). The recommended opposite is よく{噛|か}んで{食|た}べる (to chew well).

SENSE 2 — COMPETITIVE EATING:
{早食|はやぐ}い{大会|たいかい} and {早食|はやぐ}い{競争|きょうそう} refer to speed-eating contests.

RELATED WORDS:
- {大食|おおぐ}い: eating large amounts, big eater
- フードファイター: competitive eater
- {食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}: all-you-can-eat
